text: Provisioning a GPU VM in Terraform looks almost identical to provisioning any other VM — same resource types, same workflow — but there's a planning step that doesn't exist for ordinary compute: GPU capacity is scarce, and quota for GPU families is often set to zero by default. This lesson walks through requesting that quota, then writing real Terraform for an Azure NC-series VM and an AWS P-series instance.

Before touching HCL, check what you actually have. On Azure, az vm list-usage against your target region shows the current quota for a family like NCADSA100v4 — if it's at the limit, request an increase in the portal scoped to that exact region, since quota doesn't transfer between regions. On AWS, the same check happens in Service Quotas under EC2, raising the running-instance limit for P-series on-demand instances before you ever plan a training run.

On Azure, the resource is the same azurerm_linux_virtual_machine you'd use for any VM — the only thing that makes it a GPU VM is the size argument, something like Standard_NC24ads_A100_v4, which attaches a single A100 along with 24 vCPUs and roughly 220 gibibytes of RAM. Point the source image at Microsoft's ubuntu-hpc DSVM image and the NVIDIA driver and CUDA toolkit arrive already installed.

AWS follows the identical pattern with aws_instance. p4d.24xlarge gives you eight A100 GPUs connected by NVLink — the mainstream multi-GPU training instance — sitting below p5.48xlarge's eight H100s and above a single-GPU p3.2xlarge. A data source lookup for AWS's own Deep Learning AMI gets you the same pre-installed driver and CUDA stack Azure's DSVM image provides.

Two gotchas worth remembering: not every region carries every GPU family, so check availability before you write a config that assumes one exists, and GPU spot capacity gets reclaimed far more aggressively than ordinary spot capacity, because the hardware itself is scarcer. Next lesson picks up right where the VM boots: installing the driver, CUDA, and the container toolkit that makes the GPU usable from inside a container.
